papers.title: Geometry-Conditioned Hyperalignment for Generalizable EEG Decoding Across Datasets and Paradigms
papers.summary: Introduces hTSMNet, combining geometry-conditioned hyperalignment, which maps any electrode montage onto fixed scalp anchors using coordinates alone, with an SPD manifold backbone for zero-shot cross-subject and cross-dataset EEG decoding. On a leave-one-dataset-out motor-imagery benchmark across three datasets (172 subjects), it matched the strongest zero-shot comparator and achieved the highest accuracy on every dataset after minimal classifier-only calibration; the frozen model also transferred to mental workload and SSVEP but not stimulus-locked ERP, indicating generalization of band-limited oscillatory representations rather than named tasks.

papers.title: Temporal-context learning for subject-independent sleep staging with non-contact multi-frequency radar.
papers.summary: Developed a temporal-context learning model for subject-independent sleep staging using non-contact multi-frequency radar, achieving macro-F1 of 0.376 on held-out participants. Removing temporal context reduced macro-F1 by 0.072, identifying it as the main contributor among assessed components.

papers.title: Using wearable EEG to examine age trends in sleep macro- and micro-architecture across adolescence
papers.summary: Tested whether the Dreem3 wearable EEG headband can replicate established age-related trends in sleep physiology in 100 typically developing youth aged 9-26 across 3-4 nights of at-home recording. The device reproduced some expected trends, including rising NREM stage 2% and declining N3%, time in bed, and NREM delta and theta power with age, while several other associations did not reach significance.

papers.title: Multi-day recalibration-free electrophysiology interface based on carbon nanotube thin film dry electrodes.
papers.summary: Presented carbon nanotube thin-film dry electrodes synthesized via roll-to-roll floating catalyst CVD that achieved low impedance and high signal fidelity, outperforming wet electrodes. In a multichannel myoelectric interface, stable signals and task performance were maintained across 14 days without model retraining.

papers.title: Macroscale dynamics of EEG microstates constitute the periodic and aperiodic features of the neural power spectrum
papers.summary: Used orthogonal subspace projection to remove spatial projections of distinct EEG microstate configurations from high-density scalp recordings and modeled cortical generators, then spectrally parameterized the residual power. Removing these projections attenuated alpha and theta rhythms and the aperiodic 1/f background in configuration-specific ways, and microstate duration and temporal persistence correlated strongly with periodic alpha, theta, and 1/f features, supporting microstate dynamics as the time-domain source of periodic and aperiodic spectra.

papers.title: Different Pipelines, Different EEG Microstate Results: Evidence from Dementia Samples.
papers.summary: Analyzed resting-state EEG from Alzheimer's disease, frontotemporal dementia, and healthy controls using multiple microstate pipelines, showing that evidence for group differences varied substantially with temporal smoothing and clustering algorithm. Split-half reliability of microstate measures also differed across pipelines, highlighting the need for explicit pipeline validation.

papers.title: A shared slowing axis and phenotype-specific rhythms link clinical EEG to FDG-PET dementia phenotypes
papers.summary: Applied nonnegative tensor decomposition to clinical EEG from 455 patients, identifying four latent oscillatory factors that varied across FDG-PET-defined neurodegenerative phenotypes. A slowing index tracked a DLB-associated metabolic pattern, and the factors supported exploratory classification of dementia phenotypes with AUC > 0.8 for several contrasts.

papers.title: Detection of linear dependencies in EEG oscillatory sources via PARALIND and block-term decomposition: A comparative study.
papers.summary: Compared PARALIND and block-term decomposition against CANDECOMP/PARAFAC for detecting linear dependencies in EEG oscillatory sources using simulated and real data. PARALIND and BTD provided more stable factor estimates at moderate noise and disentangled overlapping sources that CP struggled to isolate, with fewer loadings in real data.

papers.title: Interictal Electroencephalographic Characteristics of the Human Centromedian Thalamic Nucleus Recorded in Focal Epilepsy.
papers.journal: Clinical neurophysiology : official journal of the International Federation of Clinical Neurophysiology
papers.summary: Analyzed interictal stereo-EEG from the centromedian thalamic nucleus and neighboring VL/VP nuclei in 33 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy and 3 non-epileptic individuals, finding state-dependent dynamics: fast/gamma activity during wakefulness and delta/theta dominance during sleep, with thalamic EEG changes preceding scalp arousal by a median 800 ms. Thalamic interictal epileptic discharges occurred in 36.4% of patients, invariably involving the CM, more often in extratemporal than temporal lobe epilepsy and not associated with surgical outcome.

papers.title: Aperiodic Exponent as an EEG Marker of Interoceptive Attention during Gastric Fullness
papers.summary: Showed that the EEG aperiodic exponent flattens after water intake to fullness consistently across individuals, accompanied by increased vagal drive to peripheral organs measured via simultaneous gastric and cardiac recordings. Changes in cortical aperiodic exponent patterns were associated with changes in gastric oscillation frequency, suggesting the exponent as a noninvasive biomarker of gastric interoceptive attention.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Neonatal Seizure Detection: A Pragmatic Evaluation of Clinical Performance Tradeoffs in Clinical EEG.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
papers.summary: Evaluated three AI-based neonatal seizure detectors on 15,343 hours of continuous EEG from 169 neonates with encephalopathy, finding all identified ≥95% of seizure-positive infants but with differing tradeoffs between seizure-level detection and false alarm burden. NSD2 had the lowest false detections (3.2/day) but detected only 35% of seizures, whereas NSD1 and Persyst-15 detected 60-63% with higher false detections for NSD1 (46/day).

papers.title: Talking Brains: Neonatal Aperiodic Activity in Resting State EEG Relates to Later Communicative Abilities
papers.summary: This study examined whether aperiodic activity in neonatal resting-state EEG relates to communicative abilities at 12 months in 50 typically developing infants, extracting aperiodic offset and exponent using the FOOOF algorithm. Quadratic regression showed an inverted U-shaped relationship between the neonatal aperiodic exponent and later communicative abilities, with both lower and higher exponent values associated with poorer outcomes and intermediate values with better abilities.

papers.title: Scalp EEG seizure warning in children under a pre-specified, locked evaluation: confound audit, structured chance levels and a negative result
papers.summary: Evaluated scalp EEG seizure warning in 21 monitored children under a pre-specified, locked protocol, finding the initial method (44% of seizures, 0.48 false alarms/hour) no better than chance. A redesigned state-conditioned scheme achieved 33% detection during cross-validation but failed to exceed structured chance in two external validation cohorts (19% detection at 0.60 false alarms/hour versus 26% chance), a negative result.

papers.title: Exploring Data Augmentation for Stroke Severity Prediction: How Generative AI Enhances EEG Signal Classification
papers.summary: Evaluated traditional oversampling (SMOTE, ADASYN) and generative augmentation (WGAN, WGAN-GP) within a hybrid pipeline of preprocessing, statistical and frequency-domain feature extraction, feature selection, and classifiers for EEG-based stroke severity prediction in 50 patients. The combination of SelectKBest, SVM, and WGAN-GP augmentation achieved the highest accuracy at 72%, outperforming the other methods.

papers.title: A Neuroscientific Prior-Guided Multi-View Network With Structured Channel Selection for EEG Emotion Recognition.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: Proposed SGA-MVTN, a neuroscientific prior-guided two-stage framework integrating a multi-view tower network with a structured genetic algorithm for topology-aware EEG channel selection in emotion recognition. Under leave-one-subject-out, full-channel MVTN achieved 87.91% on SEED and 71.09% on SEED-IV, and SGA-MVTN reduced channels by 54.84% while retaining 95.56% of full-channel accuracy.

papers.title: In-ear electroencephalography: a systematic review of technology, applications, challenges, and future directions.
papers.summary: Systematically reviewed 24 studies on in-ear (ear-EEG) technologies, documenting progress in device miniaturization and wearable design with applications in sleep monitoring, seizure detection, cognitive workload, fatigue monitoring, and emotion recognition. Remaining challenges include signal quality, spatial coverage, and motion artifacts, requiring further validation for broader clinical and real-world use.

papers.title: Capturing continuous spectrotemporal pupil--brain coupling with simultaneous wearable EEG/Eye tracking
papers.summary: Used wearable mobile EEG (MUSE) and eye tracking (Tobii Pro Glasses 3) to test whether spectrotemporal and directional pupil-brain coupling is detectable in naturalistic, continuous resting-state recordings with interoceptive attention. Cross-correlation, mutual information, and Granger causality showed frequency-dependent coupling, with lower EEG frequencies (2-12 Hz) preceding pupil dynamics by roughly 764 ms and predominantly EEG-to-pupil directionality, preserved across recording states.

papers.title: Stimulated human cortical waves: spatiotemporal dynamics across development
papers.summary: Applied a manifold-based optical flow algorithm to intracranial EEG cortico-cortical evoked potentials from single-pulse stimulation to reconstruct high-temporal-resolution cortical velocity fields, revealing hierarchical organization dominated by large-scale plane waves plus local patterns. Dominant plane wave directions aligned with white matter fiber tract orientation, velocity field singular points associated with default mode network hubs, and cortical wave speed showed a nonlinear relationship with age paralleling white matter maturation and aging.

papers.title: ScaleBrain: A Scale-Consistent Framework for EEG Foundation Models
papers.summary: Proposed ScaleBrain, a scale-consistent pre-training framework for EEG foundation models that uses multi-scale tokenization with shared temporal anchors and scale-specific reconstruction, plus axial spatio-temporal attention. On six public BCI benchmarks against 12 baselines, it achieved the highest mean balanced accuracy on five datasets and third on the remaining one with only 5.0M parameters.

papers.title: HRA-Former: Hierarchical Region-Aware Transformer with Structure-Preserving Multi-Stage Learning for EEG-Based Driver Fatigue Detection.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: Developed HRA-Former, a hierarchical region-aware Transformer with structure-preserving multi-stage learning for EEG-based driver fatigue detection, using electrode-to-region aggregation and a two-stage masked reconstruction and classification strategy. It achieved subject-dependent accuracies of 95.18% on SEED-VIG and 86.67% on an independently collected dataset, outperforming representative methods.

papers.title: A Dual-Branch Model based Federated Learning Framework for Seizure-Type Classification.
papers.journal: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
papers.summary: Proposed a dual-branch model with federated learning for automatic seizure-type classification from multi-center EEG, integrating 1DCNN complexity features and 2DCNN brain-network topological features via dynamic attention fusion and using FedProx to handle non-IID data. The framework maintained 98.42% accuracy and 94.79% macro-F1 even under extremely unbalanced data.

papers.title: Multimodal EEG-fNIRS complexity analysis can reveal the neurovascular coupling change with aging.
papers.summary: The study used simultaneous EEG-fNIRS with nonlinear entropy analysis in 20 young and 20 older adults across four cognitive tasks, finding age-related task-specific alterations in neural and hemodynamic complexity and their cross-modal relationship, suggesting dynamic reorganization of neurovascular coupling rather than uniform impairment.

papers.title: Multiscale EEG network alterations in adolescents with depressive symptoms: static-dynamic connectivity, topological features, and exploratory scalp-level network hubs.
papers.summary: Using resting-state EEG from 96 adolescents with depressive symptoms and 154 controls, the study identified multiscale network abnormalities: theta-band static hyperconnectivity, reduced dynamic flexibility, and focal topological vulnerability in prefrontal regions, with spatial overlap to neuromodulation hubs.

papers.title: Mixed Signals: Weight-Space Programming for EEG and ECG
papers.summary: Demonstrates weight-space programming by having language models read and edit the weights of EEG and ECG models, including debugging planted faults and writing network weights from scratch. In one experiment a language model matched standard gradient-descent training using 6× fewer subjects, and weight-written networks outperformed classic hand-crafted EEG pipelines (alpha power, CSP+LDA) built from the same 5 subjects.

papers.title: Electroencephalography Neurophysiology Alterations in Association with Aβ and Tau Pathology Across the Symptomatic Stages of Alzheimer's Disease Continuum: A Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional study of 73 MCI and AD participants combining resting-state EEG source analysis with Aβ- and tau-PET to relate regional proteinopathy to spectral power. Higher Aβ SUVR correlated with increased theta and decreased beta power in a subset of cortical regions, while tau positivity attenuated the amyloid-beta association in a few parietal regions.

papers.title: EEG functional connectivity as a prognostic biomarker of adaptive function in autistic people.
papers.summary: Longitudinal study of 150 autistic and 159 non-autistic participants aged 6–31 showing that EEG cortico-cortical functional connectivity metrics predicted 19-month changes in adaptive function. In 15–24-year-olds, mean degree and small-world index explained 21% and 30% of additional variance respectively (AUC up to 0.84), outperforming intelligence and autistic-feature measures.

papers.title: Temporal Dynamics of Multi-Item Working Memory Maintenance in Human Gaze Patterns and EEG
papers.summary: Recorded eye-tracking and EEG while participants maintained up to three object orientations in working memory, finding that miniature gaze patterns encoded all three items throughout the delay with load and serial-position effects, whereas EEG encoding was short-lived. Contrary to rhythmic sampling accounts, eye movements did not alternate between items and gaze encoding strength was not modulated by frontal theta.

papers.title: Cortical depth EEG-fMRI at 7T: Experimental setup and analysis pipeline to elucidate generating mechanisms of alpha oscillations.
papers.summary: The authors developed a 7T laminar EEG-fMRI pipeline with deveining to study alpha oscillations, observing negative alpha-BOLD correlations in visual cortex that were weakest in middle cortical depths after vein exclusion, consistent with superficial and deep sources of top-down alpha generation.

papers.title: Beyond Exploration: Heightened Recent Reward Reliance and Midfrontal Sensitivity to Outcome Differences in ADHD
papers.summary: Examined exploratory decision-making in 23 adults with ADHD and 27 controls using a restless four-armed bandit task with EEG across 450 trials. Groups did not differ in exploration rates or performance, but ADHD participants more strongly repeated options after high rewards and switched after low rewards, and showed greater midfrontal sensitivity to unsigned payoff changes in a 280-568 ms feedback-evoked response carried by slow activity below 2 Hz.

papers.title: Comb-Like EEG Pattern as an Early Diagnostic Clue in Maple Syrup Urine Disease (MSUD): A Systematic Review.
papers.journal: American journal of medical genetics. Part A
papers.summary: Systematic review of 18 studies (24 symptomatic cases) evaluating the comb-like EEG rhythm as a diagnostic clue in maple syrup urine disease (MSUD). Found the comb-like pattern exclusively in neonates with acute metabolic crisis (86.7% vs 0% non-neonates, p<0.0001) and associated with higher plasma leucine concentrations (median 3545 vs 1782 μmol/L, p=0.0033).

papers.title: Effects of Pore Mutations on 1/f Flicker Noise Reveal Differences in CFTR Substates.
papers.summary: Using time-frequency spectrograms and spectral analysis of single-channel CFTR recordings, the authors found 1/fα flicker noise with α=0.5 in the fully open state versus flat PSD in the closed state, distinct frequency and Hurst-exponent signatures for substates S1, S2 and F, and reproduced these findings with a transistor-based circuit model.

papers.title: Fast-Gelling, Adhesive, and Conductive Epidermal Electrode for Accurate Physiological Signal Monitoring and Real-Time Brain-Controlled Drone Flight.
papers.summary: The authors developed a fast-gelling (<5 min at room temperature) MXene/WPU/PAA conductive hydrogel epidermal electrode with strong adhesion and high conductivity, achieving sEMG and ECG signal-to-noise ratios of 36.0 dB and 30.1 dB that exceeded Ag/AgCl electrodes. The electrode also enabled scalp EEG monitoring that supported wireless drone flight control via real-time brainwave decoding.

papers.title: A high-throughput all-optical platform for mapping gene perturbations to electrophysiology
papers.summary: Developed a high-throughput all-optical electrophysiology platform combining an engineered hiPSC line (inducible NGN2, CRISPRi, Voltron2/CheRiff) with wide-field voltage imaging and automated analysis, recording ~1,500 spiking neurons at 800 Hz. Arrayed knockdown of five sodium- and potassium-channel genes produced distinct electrophysiological phenotypes, establishing a scalable platform for functional genomics.

papers.title: Side-to-side and other complex head movements as ictal signs in epilepsy: A video-EEG case series and review of literature.
papers.journal: Epileptic disorders : international epilepsy journal with videotape
papers.summary: A video-EEG case series and literature review of 17 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy showing that ictal side-to-side and complex head movements occurred in focal seizures but had no localizing or lateralizing value, with heterogeneous presumed epileptogenic zones and likely reflecting seizure propagation.

papers.title: Ethical Risks and Governance of Consumer Electroencephalography-Based Neurotechnology: Qualitative Interview Study With Expert Stakeholders
papers.summary: Conducted semi-structured interviews with 19 expert stakeholders across research, clinical practice, engineering, industry, ethics, law, and regulation in North America, Europe, and Latin America, and used reflexive thematic analysis to examine governance of consumer EEG-based neurotechnology. Five themes emerged spanning regulatory category boundaries, evidential credibility and claims-related harm, neurodata privacy and inference, layered accountability, and global equity, supporting a model of distributed oversight responsibility across actors and product lifecycle stages.

papers.title: From attention capture to responsibility attribution: Public responses to AI discrimination crises.
papers.summary: Reported two experiments comparing public responses to AI versus executive discrimination: Study 1 (N=148) found higher corporate responsibility attribution for AI discrimination but lower reputation and higher negative word-of-mouth intention for executive discrimination, with the latter result preliminary due to moderate scale reliability. Study 2 (N=30) using EEG found AI discrimination elicited larger P2 amplitude (dz=0.60) and lower frontal-central theta activity (dz=-0.43), indicating early (~first quarter-second) registration of actor cues and a separation between responsibility judgment and punishment-related responses.

papers.title: International Survey of Stereo-EEG Practices: A Comparative Analysis of Epilepsy Surgery Centers in Europe and North America.
papers.journal: Journal of clinical neurophysiology : official publication of the American Electroencephalographic Society
papers.summary: Conducted an international 39-item survey of 66 epilepsy surgery centers (38 North American, 28 European) to compare stereo-EEG practices, finding North American centers more often used robotic implantation and had higher volumes, while European centers had more SEEG experience, more dedicated readers, and more frequent SEEG-guided radiofrequency ablation. Symptomatic hemorrhage was more frequent in North America unadjusted but not after adjustment for experience and volume.

papers.title: Machine learning framework to enhance and automate cardiovascular outpatient triage for patients with atrial fibrillation.
papers.journal: BMC medical informatics and decision making
papers.summary: Developed a two-stage machine learning framework to triage 6,755 patients referred to cardiovascular care with atrial fibrillation toward specialized electrophysiology care, using demographics, comorbidities, medications, prior procedures, NLP-analyzed notes, and Holter data. Gradient Boosting Decision Trees achieved AUC 0.77, accuracy 72%, TPR 67%, and FPR 23%, and post-refinement based on clinical criteria raised TPR to 83% and increased identification of EP-direct care from 20% to 46%.

papers.title: Potential Applications of Brain-Computer Interface Technology in the Rehabilitation of Patients with Anxiety Disorders: A Narrative Review.
papers.summary: A narrative review examining the mechanistic rationale, technologies (EEG, fNIRS, rt-fMRI, invasive closed-loop), and integration of brain-computer interfaces in anxiety disorder rehabilitation, concluding that BCIs remain exploratory adjuncts limited by small single-center studies, heterogeneous protocols, and unresolved neural data governance.

papers.title: Visualization of super-selective Wada with computed tomography perfusion: toward a novel option in preoperative functional mapping.
papers.summary: Combined super-selective Wada test (ssWada) with CT perfusion (CTP) to visualize pharmacologically inactivated brain regions in 23 patients undergoing preoperative evaluation for brain tumors or drug-resistant epilepsy, and fused these data with MRI and post-SEEG CT. The approach enabled territory-based functional mapping with high spatial resolution; in the MCA superior trunk territory, repetition, naming, and reading tasks showed positive rates of approximately 70%, whereas in the inferior trunk territory, repetition and reading had high positive rates (93.8%) and naming positivity was lower (56.3%).

topic.label: EEG & Signal Methods
topic.description: EEG signal processing, sleep staging, neural time series, modeling, and practical analysis methods.
